rows.text: On a wet road the tires have less grip than on a dry one, so the distance needed to stop increases.
evidence: UK Department for Transport, Highway Code rule 227, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-highway-code/driving-in-adverse-weather-conditions-226-to-237: wet roads reduce tyre grip and increase stopping distance.

rows.text: When water cannot drain away fast enough, a film forms between tire and road, causing the wheel to lose contact and grip.
evidence: Texas Department of Transportation, Hydraulics Manual, Hydroplaning, https://www.txdot.gov/content/txdotoms/us/en/manuals/des/hyd/chapter-10--storm-drains/section-4--pavement-drainage/hydroplaning.html: when tread and pavement drainage capacity is exceeded, a water wedge can lift the tire and eliminate friction; speed and tread depth affect hydroplaning.

Georgia Department of Driver Services, Drivers Manual, Hydroplaning, https://dds.georgia.gov/drivers-manual: tires channel water away; hydroplaning can remove road contact and cause an uncontrollable skid; adequate water-channeling tread helps prevent it.

rows.text: A badly worn tread drains less water, so under the same conditions aquaplaning can start at a lower speed.
evidence: NHTSA, Tire pressure FMVSS 138, pp. V-56–V-57, https://www.nhtsa.gov/sites/nhtsa.gov/files/fmvss/tirepressure-fmvss-138.pdf: speed, tread depth and water depth affect hydroplaning; worn tread is less able to remove water.

NASA, A systematic experimental investigation of significant parameters affecting model tire hydroplaning, conclusions, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/archive/nasa/casi.ntrs.nasa.gov/19740003931.pdf: hydroplaning inception speed increases with tread depth.

Texas Department of Transportation, Hydraulics Manual, Hydroplaning, https://www.txdot.gov/content/txdotoms/us/en/manuals/des/hyd/chapter-10--storm-drains/section-4--pavement-drainage/hydroplaning.html: when tread and pavement drainage capacity is exceeded, a water wedge can lift the tire and eliminate friction; speed and tread depth affect hydroplaning.

rows.text: Tread grooves let water escape from the contact area. If drainage is insufficient, the tire can lift onto a film of water.
evidence: Texas Department of Transportation, Hydraulics Manual, Hydroplaning, https://www.txdot.gov/content/txdotoms/us/en/manuals/des/hyd/chapter-10--storm-drains/section-4--pavement-drainage/hydroplaning.html: when tread and pavement drainage capacity is exceeded, a water wedge can lift the tire and eliminate friction; speed and tread depth affect hydroplaning.

Georgia Department of Driver Services, Drivers Manual, Hydroplaning, https://dds.georgia.gov/drivers-manual: tires channel water away; hydroplaning can remove road contact and cause an uncontrollable skid; adequate water-channeling tread helps prevent it.

rows.text: The risk increases with speed, not with a reduction in speed: water has less time to escape from the contact area.
evidence: NHTSA, Tire pressure FMVSS 138, pp. V-56–V-57, https://www.nhtsa.gov/sites/nhtsa.gov/files/fmvss/tirepressure-fmvss-138.pdf: speed, tread depth and water depth affect hydroplaning; worn tread is less able to remove water.

Pennsylvania Driver’s Manual, Managing Speed, https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmv/driver-services/pennsylvania-drivers-manual/online-drivers-manual/everyday-driving-skills/managing-speed: faster tyres are less effective at clearing water; reducing speed reduces hydroplaning.

rows.text: Aquaplaning removes grip and can cause skidding and loss of control instead of reducing them.
evidence: Texas Department of Transportation, Hydraulics Manual, Hydroplaning, https://www.txdot.gov/content/txdotoms/us/en/manuals/des/hyd/chapter-10--storm-drains/section-4--pavement-drainage/hydroplaning.html: when tread and pavement drainage capacity is exceeded, a water wedge can lift the tire and eliminate friction; speed and tread depth affect hydroplaning.

Georgia Department of Driver Services, Drivers Manual, Hydroplaning, https://dds.georgia.gov/drivers-manual: tires channel water away; hydroplaning can remove road contact and cause an uncontrollable skid; adequate water-channeling tread helps prevent it.

rows.text: Tread depth matters: a badly worn tread drains less water, increasing the risk of aquaplaning.
evidence: NHTSA, Tire pressure FMVSS 138, pp. V-56–V-57, https://www.nhtsa.gov/sites/nhtsa.gov/files/fmvss/tirepressure-fmvss-138.pdf: speed, tread depth and water depth affect hydroplaning; worn tread is less able to remove water.

rows.text: Snow and ice reduce grip. A moderate speed gives the rider more chance to control the vehicle and stop.
evidence: UK Department for Transport, Highway Code rules 230–231, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-highway-code/driving-in-adverse-weather-conditions-226-to-237: greater stopping distance on snow and ice; slow down and accelerate, brake and steer gently, especially on bends.

rows.text: Stopping distance increases on snow or ice, so a larger gap gives more room to stop.
evidence: UK Department for Transport, Highway Code rules 230–231, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-highway-code/driving-in-adverse-weather-conditions-226-to-237: greater stopping distance on snow and ice; slow down and accelerate, brake and steer gently, especially on bends.

rows.text: With little grip, sudden acceleration can make the wheels slip. Accelerate gradually.
evidence: UK Department for Transport, Highway Code rules 230–231, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-highway-code/driving-in-adverse-weather-conditions-226-to-237: greater stopping distance on snow and ice; slow down and accelerate, brake and steer gently, especially on bends.

Oregon DMV, Commercial Driver Manual §2.19, https://www.oregon.gov/odot/DMV/Pages/Online_CDL_Manual_2/Section_2.aspx: excessive acceleration can spin drive wheels and cause a skid, particularly on ice or snow.
Georgia Department of Driver Services, Commercial Drivers Manual §2.2, https://dds.georgia.gov/section-22: accelerate gradually when traction is poor; excessive power can spin the drive wheels.

rows.text: Braking hard on snow or ice can cause a skid. Slow down in good time and brake gently.
evidence: UK Department for Transport, Highway Code rules 230–231, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-highway-code/driving-in-adverse-weather-conditions-226-to-237: greater stopping distance on snow and ice; slow down and accelerate, brake and steer gently, especially on bends.

rows.text: Accelerating fully when moving off can make the wheels slip on a slippery surface; accelerate gently.
evidence: UK Department for Transport, Highway Code rules 230–231, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-highway-code/driving-in-adverse-weather-conditions-226-to-237: greater stopping distance on snow and ice; slow down and accelerate, brake and steer gently, especially on bends.

Georgia Department of Driver Services, Commercial Drivers Manual §2.2, https://dds.georgia.gov/section-22: accelerate gradually when traction is poor; excessive power can spin the drive wheels.

rows.text: Sudden steering on snow or ice can cause loss of grip and control. Anticipate the obstacle and maneuver smoothly.
evidence: UK Department for Transport, Highway Code rules 230–231, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-highway-code/driving-in-adverse-weather-conditions-226-to-237: greater stopping distance on snow and ice; slow down and accelerate, brake and steer gently, especially on bends.

rows.text: Grip is more easily lost on a slippery bend: slow down before the bend and take it carefully.
evidence: UK Department for International Development, Motorcycle Rider Training Instructor Manual, pp. 56–58, https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5fa19888e90e07042c1e10f0/Transaidetal-2020-InstructorsManualCBCMotorcycleRiderTraining-Generic-AfCAP-RAF2114A-190524__1_.pdf: slippery surfaces reduce traction; slow before curves and avoid sudden inputs.

rows.text: With less grip, more distance is needed to stop. A larger gap helps you stop if the vehicle ahead slows down.
evidence: UK Department for International Development, Motorcycle Rider Training Instructor Manual, pp. 56–58, https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5fa19888e90e07042c1e10f0/Transaidetal-2020-InstructorsManualCBCMotorcycleRiderTraining-Generic-AfCAP-RAF2114A-190524__1_.pdf: slippery surfaces reduce traction; slow before curves and avoid sudden inputs.

UK Department for Transport, Highway Code rule 227, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-highway-code/driving-in-adverse-weather-conditions-226-to-237: wet roads reduce tyre grip and increase stopping distance.

rows.text: A moderate, as steady as possible speed reduces the need for sudden maneuvers, which can cause skids on a slippery surface.
evidence: UK Department for International Development, Motorcycle Rider Training Instructor Manual, pp. 56–58, https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5fa19888e90e07042c1e10f0/Transaidetal-2020-InstructorsManualCBCMotorcycleRiderTraining-Generic-AfCAP-RAF2114A-190524__1_.pdf: slippery surfaces reduce traction; slow before curves and avoid sudden inputs.

rows.text: Sudden acceleration can make the wheels slip. Travel slowly and accelerate gradually on a slippery surface.
evidence: UK Department for International Development, Motorcycle Rider Training Instructor Manual, pp. 56–58, https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5fa19888e90e07042c1e10f0/Transaidetal-2020-InstructorsManualCBCMotorcycleRiderTraining-Generic-AfCAP-RAF2114A-190524__1_.pdf: slippery surfaces reduce traction; slow before curves and avoid sudden inputs.

Georgia Department of Driver Services, Commercial Drivers Manual §2.2, https://dds.georgia.gov/section-22: accelerate gradually when traction is poor; excessive power can spin the drive wheels.

evidence: UK Department for International Development, Motorcycle Rider Training Instructor Manual, pp. 56–58, https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5fa19888e90e07042c1e10f0/Transaidetal-2020-InstructorsManualCBCMotorcycleRiderTraining-Generic-AfCAP-RAF2114A-190524__1_.pdf: slippery surfaces reduce traction; slow before curves and avoid sudden inputs.

rows.text: Sudden handlebar movements can cause loss of grip. On a slippery surface, maneuvers must be smooth and gradual.
evidence: UK Department for International Development, Motorcycle Rider Training Instructor Manual, pp. 56–58, https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5fa19888e90e07042c1e10f0/Transaidetal-2020-InstructorsManualCBCMotorcycleRiderTraining-Generic-AfCAP-RAF2114A-190524__1_.pdf: slippery surfaces reduce traction; slow before curves and avoid sudden inputs.

rows.text: Water on the road reduces grip between tire and asphalt, making braking and control more difficult.
evidence: UK Department for Transport, Highway Code rule 227, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-highway-code/driving-in-adverse-weather-conditions-226-to-237: wet roads reduce tyre grip and increase stopping distance.

rows.text: Leaves, especially when wet, form a slippery layer between tire and road and can reduce grip.
evidence: London Fire Brigade, Motorbikes, https://www.london-fire.gov.uk/safety/road-safety/motorbikes/: wet leaves and diesel spills are motorcycle skid hazards.

rows.text: Snow and ice make the road slippery: wheels have less grip and can slip more easily.
evidence: UK Department for Transport, Highway Code rules 230–231, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-highway-code/driving-in-adverse-weather-conditions-226-to-237: greater stopping distance on snow and ice; slow down and accelerate, brake and steer gently, especially on bends.

rows.text: Oil forms a slippery layer on the asphalt and reduces tire grip on the road.
evidence: UK Department for Transport, Highway Code rule 227, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-highway-code/driving-in-adverse-weather-conditions-226-to-237: wet roads reduce tyre grip and increase stopping distance.

rows.text: Low speed does not itself make the road less grippy. On a wet road, higher speed increases the risk of aquaplaning.
evidence: NHTSA, Tire pressure FMVSS 138, pp. V-56–V-57, https://www.nhtsa.gov/sites/nhtsa.gov/files/fmvss/tirepressure-fmvss-138.pdf: speed, tread depth and water depth affect hydroplaning; worn tread is less able to remove water.
